skills.name: construct_incidence_correspondence
skills.description: Form a closed subscheme of a product of parameter spaces that encodes a geometric relation such as tangency, incidence, or containment.
skills.preconditions: Parameter spaces for families of varieties are given together with a relation describable by polynomial equations.
skills.postconditions: Obtains an incidence variety whose points correspond exactly to tuples satisfying the prescribed relation.
skills.example: Consider the set of pairs consisting of a line in the projective plane and a point lying on that line; this defines a closed subscheme of the product of the space of lines and the plane.

skills.name: compute_chow_ring_product
skills.description: Perform intersection product calculations in the Chow ring of a smooth projective variety using known divisor classes.
skills.preconditions: The Chow ring of the variety has a known presentation and the divisor classes representing the conditions are identified.
skills.postconditions: Produces the class of the intersection, from which degrees and other numerical invariants can be extracted.
skills.example: In the projective plane, intersect the class of a line with itself; the result is the class of a point.

skills.name: apply_bezout_theorem_for_tangency
skills.description: Use Bézout’s theorem to compute the total intersection number of hypersurfaces, incorporating appropriate multiplicities when tangency occurs.
skills.preconditions: Two hypersurfaces in projective space are given with known degrees, and the intersection is proper after accounting for tangency multiplicities.
skills.postconditions: Gives the total intersection number, counting each solution with its appropriate multiplicity.
skills.example: Compute the intersection number of a conic and a line when the line is tangent to the conic, counting the tangency with the appropriate multiplicity.

skills.name: verify_finite_etale_via_jacobian
skills.description: Check that a morphism is finite étale at a point by confirming that the Jacobian matrix has maximal rank and that the fiber is zero‑dimensional.
skills.preconditions: A morphism between varieties is presented explicitly by polynomial maps, and a point in the source is specified.
skills.postconditions: Concludes that the morphism is unramified and flat at that point, hence étale locally.
skills.example: For the map (x, y) ↦ (x², y²) from affine plane to itself, verify étaleness away from the coordinate axes by checking that the Jacobian determinant does not vanish.

skills.name: compute_degree_of_projection_map
skills.description: Determine the degree of a projection from an incidence variety to one factor by counting points in a generic fiber.
skills.preconditions: An incidence variety is defined as a closed subscheme of a product, together with the projection onto a chosen factor, and the projection is known to be finite.
skills.postconditions: Provides the integer degree, i.e., the cardinality of a generic fiber of the projection.
skills.example: Project the incidence variety of pairs (line, point on line) onto the space of lines; a generic fiber consists of a single point, so the degree is one.

skills.name: use_lang_weil_estimates_for_point_counts
skills.description: Apply the Lang–Weil estimate to bound the number of rational points on a geometrically irreducible variety over a finite field in terms of its dimension and degree.
skills.preconditions: A geometrically irreducible variety defined over a finite field is given together with its dimension and degree.
skills.postconditions: Yields an approximation of the point count up to an error term of order the field size raised to one less than the dimension.
skills.example: Estimate the number of points on a smooth plane cubic over a large prime field using its degree and dimension.

skills.name: pass_to_generic_fiber_via_flatness
skills.description: Use generic flatness to replace a family by its generic fiber, ensuring that properties verified on the generic fiber hold over a dense open subset of the base.
skills.preconditions: A morphism of finite type between Noetherian schemes is given.
skills.postconditions: Identifies a dense open subset of the base where the morphism is flat, allowing reduction to the generic fiber for further analysis.
skills.example: For a family of curves parametrized by a line, find an open set where all fibers are smooth by invoking generic flatness.

skills.name: apply_schwartz_zippel_to_estimate_fiber_sizes
skills.description: Use the Schwartz–Zippel lemma to bound the probability that a random specialization of variables satisfies a nonzero polynomial, thereby estimating the size of fibers over finite fields.
skills.preconditions: A nonzero polynomial in several variables over a finite field is given, together with a random choice of values for a subset of the variables.
skills.postconditions: Provides an upper bound on the proportion of specializations that lie in the zero set, useful for estimating average fiber cardinalities.
skills.example: Estimate how often a random pair (a, b) in a finite field satisfies a·b = 0 by applying the Schwartz–Zippel bound.

skills.name: employ_inclusion_exclusion_on_component_counts
skills.description: Apply the inclusion–exclusion principle to express the count of components satisfying multiple conditions in terms of counts for individual and intersecting conditions.
skills.preconditions: A finite collection of closed subsets of a variety is given, and the goal is to count components meeting all of them.
skills.postconditions: Produces a formula combining individual component counts and counts of their intersections to obtain the desired total.
skills.example: Count the number of lines in the plane that pass through at least one of a pair of given points by subtracting the line that passes through both.

skills.name: translate_average_over_finite_fields_to_geometric_degree
skills.description: Relate the limit of average numbers of rational points over growing finite fields to the geometric degree of a generically finite morphism.
skills.preconditions: A morphism of varieties that is generically finite is given, and one considers the average size of fibers over rational points of the base as the field size grows.
skills.postconditions: Concludes that the limit of the average fiber cardinality equals the degree of the morphism.
skills.example: For the projection from a curve embedded in a product to one factor, the average number of points in fibers over large finite fields approaches the degree of the projection.
